- Validate that event end times do not precede start times.

commitResults.messageTitle: Format code to comply with SE-EDU coding standard
commitResults.messageBody:
Several lines across the codebase exceed the 120-character maximum line
length limit, and some Javadoc tag descriptions lack terminal
punctuation.

The project requires adherence to the SE-EDU Java Coding Standard
(Basic + Intermediate rules) to maintain high code readability,
consistent layout, and clean documentation generation.

Let's,
* wrap lines exceeding 120 characters with 8-space continuation indents
* add terminal punctuation to all @param, @return, and @throws tags
* format long boolean conditional expressions and constructor
  signatures across Braun, Ui, Storage, DateTimeUtil, and Task classes

Following these layout rules ensures compliance with the course coding
standard and keeps source files clean and readable.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add seedu-java-coding-standard skill
commitResults.messageBody:
The project needs a formalized definition of the SE-EDU Java Coding
Standard so coding style rules can be referenced consistently.

Creating a dedicated skill enables autonomous agents and developers to
verify Java conventions against a standardized specification.

Let's add the seedu-java-coding-standard skill detailing naming,
layout, statement, and Javadoc rules from SE-EDU conventions.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add seedu-git-standard skill
commitResults.messageBody:
The project needs a clear standard for Git commit messages and branch
naming conventions based on course guidelines.

Establishing this skill ensures all future commits adhere to the
SE-EDU Git conventions consistently.

Let's add the seedu-git-standard skill specifying subject line format,
imperative mood, 72-character body wrapping, and commit structure.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update AGENTS.md to mandate SE-EDU standards
commitResults.messageBody:
Agent guidelines do not currently enforce the SE-EDU Java coding

Explicit instructions in the agent prompt ensure that future code
modifications and commits automatically adhere to both standards.

Let's update AGENTS.md to mandate compliance with the
seedu-java-coding-standard and seedu-git-standard skills.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add find command to search tasks by keyword
commitResults.messageBody:
Users currently have no way to search for specific tasks without
scrolling through the entire list of tasks.

Providing a search facility allows users to quickly locate relevant
tasks by querying a keyword or phrase against task descriptions.

Let's,
* add handleFind to Braun to filter tasks matching the given keyword
* add showMatchingTasks to Ui to display matching tasks or feedback
* update unknown command guidance to include the find command
* add JUnit unit tests in UiTest covering matching and empty results
* expand ui-test-plan.md with 4 automated test cases for find

Case-insensitive substring matching is used so users can find tasks
without needing to recall the exact letter casing.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JavaFX graphical user interface (Level-10)
commitResults.messageBody:
Users currently interact with Braun exclusively through a text-based
console interface, which lacks visual hierarchy, avatars, and modern
window management.

Providing a Graphical User Interface (GUI) enhances interactivity and
brings Braun's late-night supernatural talk show persona to life with
distinct chat bubbles, portrait avatars, and responsive input.

Let's,
* configure org.openjfx.javafxplugin in build.gradle with JavaFX 21
* set application mainClass to braun.Launcher for fat JAR compatibility
* add getResponse and getWelcomeMessage to Braun to bridge GUI queries
* add message formatters and showResponse to Ui for dual GUI/CLI use
* create Launcher and Main entry points for JavaFX application bootstrap
* create MainWindow controller and DialogBox custom control with FXML
* design 1970s supernatural CRT TV late-night theme in main.css
* generate thematic avatar assets for Braun and Daydream Inc. Explorer
* expand test suite with BraunTest to verify GUI response generation

The CLI console loop and test runner remain completely intact and
fully backwards-compatible.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add assertions to document assumptions
commitResults.messageBody:
The application lacks runtime assertion checks for critical internal
invariants, such as non-null model inputs, valid array indices, and
injected FXML controls.

Documenting and enforcing these assumptions with Java assertions detects
logic regressions early in development and clarifies developer intent.

Let's,
* enable assertions for test and run tasks in build.gradle
* assert non-null paths, storage, and collections in Braun constructor
* assert non-null inputs and valid task index ranges during execution
* assert non-null tasks and parsed instances in Storage
* assert non-null dates in DateTimeUtil
* assert injected FXML controls and valid instances in GUI controllers

commitResults.messageTitle: Refactor methods to improve code quality
commitResults.messageBody:
The codebase contains duplicated task index parsing across multiple
command handlers and magic literal delimiters across parsing layers.

Consolidating index parsing into a reusable helper and extracting
type constants improves readability, adheres to SLAP, and reduces code
duplication.

Let's,
* extract command keywords and delimiter constants in Braun
* add parseTaskIndex helper to unify validation across mark and delete
* extract file delimiter and task type constants in Storage
* refactor parseTask into sub-parsers for todo, deadline, and event

commitResults.messageTitle: Process task collections with Java streams
commitResults.messageBody:
Task queries and formatting methods rely on imperative loops to filter
and transform task lists into formatted display strings.

Refactoring collection processing to use Java streams and lambda
pipelines improves declarative clarity, conciseness, and readability.

Let's,
* use stream filter and collector pipelines in date and find queries
* stream task entities to serialized file lines in Storage save method
* use IntStream and Collectors.joining for task list formatting in Ui

commitResults.messageTitle: Support multi-keyword and date search in find
commitResults.messageBody:
The find command only supports exact single-substring queries against
task descriptions, preventing users from searching across multiple
keywords, exact quoted phrases, or scheduled dates and times.

Enhancing find to parse multi-word queries with OR semantics, handle
quoted phrases, and match across task strings allows flexible discovery
of tasks by description, date, time, and type.

Let's,
* parse search queries into tokens and quoted phrase terms in Braun
* match tasks if any search term appears in display or storage strings
* add unit tests for multi-keyword, phrase, and date searching
* update UI test plan with BetterSearch cases and update User Guide

commitResults.messageTitle: Enhance GUI with error styling and responsiveness
commitResults.messageBody:
User and chatbot interactions share uniform visual styling regardless
of message status, and fixed dimensions restrict content expansion
during window resizing.

Introducing distinct crimson error styling provides immediate visual
feedback for failed commands, while dynamic width bindings ensure dialog
bubbles and container content respond smoothly to window resizing.

Let's,
* add braun-error-dialog CSS theme for broadcast error transmissions
* bind dialogContainer and dialog label widths for responsive resizing
* retain input focus automatically across broadcast command submissions
* remove max dimension constraints from MainWindow layout AnchorPane

commitResults.messageTitle: Add duplicate task and delimiter error handling
commitResults.messageBody:
The application allows adding duplicate tasks with identical details
and ignores duplicate command delimiters, leading to bloated task lists
and ambiguous scheduling parameters.

Implementing duplicate task rejection and strict delimiter validation
ensures scheduling integrity and provides helpful broadcast feedback.

Let's,
* implement equals and hashCode across Task, Todo, Deadline, and Event
* reject duplicate task additions in Braun addTask method
* reject duplicate /by, /from, and /to delimiters in command inputs
* add comprehensive unit tests in BraunTest, TodoTest, and DeadlineTest
